title: Calibration Conductor: run lifecycle, artifact visibility, and SLO hooks for quant profiles
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Summary:
Build a Calibration Conductor experience in Redwood Console that coordinates quantization runs (FP8/INT8), exposes provenance and accuracy validation, enforces retention/TTL and RBAC, and wires SLO hooks so Platform/ML teams can automate rollouts when profile quality is acceptable. This ticket covers orchestration UX, artifact lifecycle policy decisions, runtime signals for SLO-driven promotion, and auditability for regulated customers.

Problem context:
- Teams run large calibration sweeps that produce many artifacts (calibration traces, quant profiles, evaluation reports). Without centralized orchestration, runs are fragmented across infra, hard to find in Console, and retention rules are inconsistent which causes storage bloat and compliance risks.
- We need clear policies for what to keep immutable (production-promoted profiles + eval snapshots), what to TTL, and who can view/promote/restore artifacts.
- Accuracy validation must be integrated with run metadata (dataset, seed, model-commit, config) and surface explainability metrics (per-layer quant error, calibration curve, downstream eval loss) so PMs/ML teams can approve profiles for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Goals / scope:
1) Orchestration: a "Conductor" abstraction in Console to start/observe/cancel calibration jobs, show live progress and job shards, and allow re-running with exact provenance.
2) Artifacts: define two classes - ephemeral (fast tracing artifacts, logs) and canonical (quant_profile, eval_report, golden_trace). Canonical artifacts must be immutable, signed, and retained longer (default 180d) with tenant override. Ephemeral TTL default 7d.
3) RBAC & visibility: job-level roles: viewer, runner, promoter. Implement UI controls to restrict promotion and download of canonical profiles. Audit trail of promotions with actor, timestamp, commit.
4) SLO hooks & automation: expose webhooks and console rules that evaluate eval metrics against SLO gates (e.g., <1% BLEU loss, <2% latency regression) to auto-promote or mark for manual review.
5) Explainability & validation: surface per-layer quantization deltas, histogram drift, and a small downstream benchmark to validate quality.

Design decisions and trade-offs so far:
- TTL defaults: chose 7d ephemeral / 180d canonical to balance storage vs reproducibility. Can be overridden per-project. Trade-off: shorter TTL reduces storage but harms reproducibility for infrequent audits.
- Immutable canonical artifacts: signing adds complexity (KMS integration) but is required for compliance customers—scope includes stubbed signing v1 now, full HSM path in Private delivery.
- Auto-promotion vs manual gating: we will support both. Auto-promotion requires conservative default SLOs and explicit opt-in. Manual gating is default for first release to avoid regressions.

Open implementation tasks:
- Implement artifact immutability stamp + KMS stub (ENG-44990) [blocked by KMS onboarding for Private].
- Console: job list + detail + promote button with permission checks (ENG-45321).
- Backend: TTL GC worker and tenant override APIs (ENG-45112).
- Eval: define canonical downstream benchmark suite and baseline profiles (PM-36501).

Acceptance criteria:
- Users can create a calibration job from Console with config, target model commit, and dataset reference.
- Job progress observable in Console with per-shard logs and percentage completion.
- Artifacts are categorized and stored with TTLs; canonical artifacts carry an immutable stamp and are retained per policy.
- RBAC enforces promoter role for promotion/download of canonical profiles; promotions are audit-logged.
- SLO rule can be defined in Console and triggers a webhook when a job's eval_report passes or fails the gate.
- A minimal explainability panel shows per-layer quant error and an aggregate quality score.

Acceptance testing steps:
1) Kick off an INT8 calibration for gpt-small using synthetic dataset; verify ephemeral artifacts are GC'd after TTL in a test tenant.
2) Promote a canonical profile as promoter; verify audit entry with actor and checksum.
3) Configure SLO to auto-promote if eval loss < 1%; run a calibration that meets condition and assert webhook fired and profile promoted.
4) Validate UI shows layer-level histograms and delta table for selected artifacts.

Risks & mitigations:
- Storage growth: monitor artifact ingestion and add backpressure / run-level quotas; early telemetry to assess 90th percentile artifact sizes.
- Incorrect auto-promote configs: default to manual and require explicit opt-in; show clear warning in Console.
- Compliance gaps (signing): implement signing stub with audit trail; delay HSM path to Private delivery.

Metrics to track post-launch:
- Time-to-promotion (manual and auto) for calibration runs
- Artifact storage usage per tenant and percent canonical vs ephemeral
- Number of runs auto-promoted vs blocked by SLOs
- Incidents related to bad promoted profiles (regressions)
